metadata.title: A Combination of Downward Continuation and Local Approximation for Harmonic Potentials

extraction_notes.note: The proof of Proposition 6.3 invokes 'the scalar localization result from Proposition \ref{prop:loc}', which points to itself; the intended target is Proposition 4.2 (prop:loc1). Added a named edge PrP1 -> PP4; no self-supporting ref edge was created.

Equation (2.15) repeats (1.4) verbatim (now as an approximation on the subset tilde Gamma_r). Both are numbered environment facts, so both were kept as equation nodes with separate definition nodes, rather than merging via also_stated_at.

Remark 4.4 states a relaxed version of Theorem 4.3 with only a sketched proof ('follows in a very similar manner'); kept as a remark with rigor semi_formal instead of splitting into a claim and proof.
The numerical setup of Section 5 (data generation, grids, parameter ranges, tables of errors) and observations (2)-(4) were not made nodes; only observations (1) and (5) are kept as numerical claims.

nodes.statement: {U_N^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}={T}_N[F_1^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1}]+{\tilde{W}}_N[F_2^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2}],}

nodes.name: First error splitting
nodes.statement: &\|U^+ - U_N^{\varepsilon}\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)} \\&\leq \|U^+ - {T}_{N}[F_1]-\tilde{W}_{N}[F_2]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}+\|{T}_{N}[F_1-F_1^{\varepsilon_1}]+\tilde{W}_{N}[F_2-F_2^{\varepsilon_2}]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}\nonumber \\&\leq \|(1-{T}_{N}{T}^{up}-\tilde{W}_{N})[U^+]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}+\varepsilon_1\|{T}_{N}[E_1]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}+\varepsilon_2\|\tilde{W}_{N}[E_2]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}.\nonumber
nodes.label: eqn:errorest2

nodes.name: Splitting of the approximation error term
nodes.statement: & \|(1-{T}_{N}{T}^{up}-\tilde{W}_{N})[U^+]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)} \\&\leq \frac{1}{2}\|(1-{T}_{N}{T}^{up})[U^+]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}+ \frac{1}{2}\left\|\int_{\Omega_r}\tilde{\Psi}_N(\cdot,y)U^+(y)d\omega(y)\right\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}\nonumber \\&\quad\, +\frac{1}{2}\left\|U^+(x)-\int_{\Omega_r}\tilde{\Phi}_N(\cdot,y)U^+(y)d\omega(y)\right\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}+ \left\|\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\cdot,\rho)}\tilde{\Psi}_N(\cdot,y)U^+(y)d\omega(y)\right\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}.\nonumber
nodes.label: eqn:errorest22

nodes.name: Spectral bound of approximation error term
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} & \|(1-{T}_{N}{T}^{up}-\tilde{W}_{N})[U^+]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)} \\&\leq \frac{1}{2}\left\|\sum_{n=0}^\infty\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}(1-{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n)\big(U_r^+\big)^\wedge(n,k)\frac{1}{r}Y_{n,k}\right\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)} \\&\quad+\frac{1}{2}\left\|\sum_{n=0}^\infty\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}\tilde{\Psi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\big(U_r^+\big)^\wedge(n,k)\frac{1}{r}Y_{n,k}\right\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)} \\&\quad+\frac{1}{2}\left\|\sum_{n=0}^\infty\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}(1-\tilde{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n))\big(U_r^+\big)^\wedge(n,k)\frac{1}{r}Y_{n,k}\right\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)} \\&\quad+\left\|\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\tilde{\Psi}_{N}(\cdot,y) U^+(y)d\omega(y)\right\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)} \\&\leq\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\frac{\big|1-\tilde{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)\big|}{2\big(n+\frac{1}{2}\big)^s}\|U^+\|_{\mathcal{H}_s(\Omega_r)}+\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\frac{\big|1-{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\sigma_n\big|}{2\big(n+\frac{1}{2}\big)^s}\|U^+\|_{\mathcal{H}_s(\Omega_r)} \\&\quad+\frac{1}{2}\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\big|\tilde{\Psi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\big|\|U^+\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}+2\sqrt{2}\pi r^2\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_{N}\big\|_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}\|U^+\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eqn:errorest23

nodes.statement: \inf_{n=0,\ldots, \lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{\beta_N\frac{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{2(N+1)}}{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2}+( \lfloor\kappa N\rfloor+1)^2}{{\alpha}_{N,n}}&=\mathcal{O}\left(N^{-2(1+\delta)}\right),\quad \textit{ for }N\to\infty.

nodes.statement: \lim_{N\to\infty}\left\|U^+-U_ {N}^{\varepsilon}\right\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}=0.
nodes.label: eqn:convres

nodes.name: Shannon-type symbols
nodes.statement: \big(\Phi_N^{Sh}\big)^\wedge(n)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}\frac{1}{\sigma_n},&n\leq N,\\0,&\textnormal{else},\end{array}\right.\qquad \big(\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^{Sh}\big)^\wedge(n)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}1,&n\leq \lfloor\kappa N\rfloor,\\0,&\textnormal{else},\end{array}\right.

nodes.name: Functional value at Shannon kernels
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}(\Phi_N^{Sh},\tilde{\Psi}_N^{Sh})&=\beta_N\sum_{n=0}^{N}\frac{1}{\sigma_n^2}+8\pi^2 r^4\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_N^{Sh}\big\|^2_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])} \\&\leq \beta_N\frac{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{2(N+1)}}{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{2}}+8\pi^2\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\left(\frac{2n+1}{4\pi}\right)^2\left\|P_n\right\|^2_{L^2([-1,1])}\nonumber \\&= \beta_N\frac{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{2(N+1)}}{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{2}}+(\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor+1)^2.\nonumber
nodes.label: eqn:shannonest

nodes.name: Bound by the functional
nodes.statement: \tilde{\alpha}_{N,n}\big(1-\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\big)^2&\leq\mathcal{F}(\Phi_N,\tilde{\Psi}_N)\leq \mathcal{F}(\Phi_N^{Sh},\tilde{\Psi}_N^{Sh}) \\&\leq \beta_N\frac{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{2(N+1)}}{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{2}}+(\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor+1)^2,\nonumber

nodes.name: Rate for $1-\tilde{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)$
nodes.statement: \big|1-\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\big|= \mathcal{O}(N^{-1-\delta}),
nodes.label: eqn:conphij

nodes.name: Vanishing of first error term
nodes.statement: \lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\frac{|1-\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)|}{(n+\frac{1}{2})^{s}}=0,

nodes.name: Vanishing of third error term
nodes.statement: \lim_{N\to\infty}\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\left|\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\right|\leq C\lim_{N\to\infty}\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{N}=0.

nodes.name: Bound for wavelet-symbol term
nodes.statement: \left\|\sum_{n=0}^\infty\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}\tilde{\Psi}_{N}^\wedge(n)F_r^\wedge(n,k)\frac{1}{r}Y_{n,k}\right\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}^2\leq \mathcal{O}(N^{-2\delta})+C\sum_{n=N+1}^{\lfloor \kappa N\rfloor}\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}\left|F_r^\wedge(n,k)\right|^2,

nodes.name: Remaining localization terms
nodes.statement: \Bigg\|\,\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\tilde{\Psi}_{N}(\cdot,y) U^+(y)d\omega(y)\Bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}, \qquad \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2\Bigg\|\,\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\tilde{\Psi}_{N}(\cdot,y) E_2(y)d\omega(y)\Bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}
nodes.label: eqn:altterms

nodes.name: Localization estimate via Shannon kernel
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\Bigg\|\,\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\tilde{\Psi}_{N}(\cdot,y) U^+(y)d\omega(y)\Bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)} \\&\leq\Bigg\|\,\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\tilde{\Psi}^{Sh}_{N}(\cdot,y) U^+(y)d\omega(y)\Bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)} \\&\quad\,+\Bigg\|\,\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\left(\tilde{\Psi}^{Sh}_{N}(\cdot,y)-\tilde{\Psi}_{N}(\cdot,y)\right) U^+(y)d\omega(y)\Bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)} \\&\leq\Bigg\|\,\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\tilde{\Psi}^{Sh}_{N}(\cdot,y) U^+(y)d\omega(y)\Bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)} \\&\quad\,+2\pi r^2\|\tilde{\Psi}^{Sh}_{N}-\tilde{\Psi}_{N}\|_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])} \|U^+\|_{L^1(\Omega_r)}, \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eqn:locest

nodes.name: Distance to Shannon kernel
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\big\|\tilde{\Psi}^{Sh}_{N}-\tilde{\Psi}_{N}\big\|_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}^2 \\&\leq\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\left(\frac{2n+1}{4\pi}\right)^2\left|\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)-\left(\tilde{\Psi}^{Sh}_N\right)^\wedge(n)\right|^2\|P_n\|_{L^2([-1,1])}^2 \\&\leq\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{2n+1}{8\pi^2}\left|\left|\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)-1\right|+\left|{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n-1\right|\chi_{[0,N]}(n)\right|^2 \\&=\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{2n+1}{8\pi^2}\mathcal{O}\left(N^{-2(1+\delta)}\right)=\mathcal{O}\left(N^{-2\delta}\right). \end{aligned}

nodes.name: Filtered minimizing functional
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{Filter}(\Phi_N,\tilde{\Psi}_N)=&\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor \kappa N\rfloor}\tilde{\alpha}_{N,n}\big|K_N^\wedge(n)-\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\big|^2+\sum_{n=0}^{N}\alpha_{N,n}\big|K_N^\wedge(n)-{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\sigma_n\big|^2 \\&+\beta_N\sum_{n=0}^{N}\big|\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\big|^2+8\pi^2 r^4\left\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\right\|^2_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])},\nonumber
nodes.label: eqn:mineq3

nodes.name: Filtered kernel
nodes.statement: \tilde{\Phi}_{N}^{Filter}(x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}K_N^\wedge(n)Y_{n,k}\left(\frac{x}{|x|}\right)Y_{n,k}\left(\frac{y}{|y|}\right).

nodes.name: Normalized localization measure
nodes.statement: \frac{\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\big\|_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}}{\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\big\|_{L^2([-1,1])}}.
nodes.label: eqn:altloc

nodes.name: Parameter growth condition (Lemma 4.5)
nodes.statement: \inf_{n=0,\ldots, \lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{\beta_N\frac{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{2(N+1)}}{1-\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2}+( \lfloor\kappa N\rfloor+1)^2}{{\alpha}_{N,n}}&=\mathcal{O}\left(N^{-2(1+\delta)}\right),\quad \textit{ for }N\to\infty.
nodes.label: eqn:ass11

nodes.name: Asymptotic localization of $\tilde{\Psi}_N$
nodes.statement: \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\big\|^2_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}}{\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\big\|^2_{L^2([-1,1])}}=0.
nodes.label: eqn:optloc2

nodes.name: Cantelli bound for leakage
nodes.statement: \frac{\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\big\|^2_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}}{\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\big\|^2_{L^2([-1,1])}}&=\int_{-1}^{1-\rho}F_N(t)dt=P_N(t< 1-\rho)=1-P_N\big(t-E_N(t)\geq 1-\rho-E_N(t)\big)\nonumber \\&\leq \frac{V_N(t)}{V_N(t)+ (1-\rho-E_N(t))^2},

nodes.name: First moment of $|\tilde{\Psi}_N|^2$
nodes.statement: \int_{-1}^1 t|\tilde{\Psi}_N(t)|^2 dt&= \frac{1}{r^2} \sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\sum_{m=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{2n+1}{4\pi}\frac{2m+1}{4\pi}\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(m)\int_{-1}^1tP_n(t)P_m(t)dt \\&=\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{2n+1}{16\pi^2r^2}\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)\left(n\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n-1)+(n+1)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n+1)\right)\int_{-1}^1|P_n(t)|^2 dt\nonumber \\&=\frac{1}{8\pi^2r^2}\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}n\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n-1)+(n+1)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n+1).\nonumber
nodes.label: eqn:et1

nodes.name: Asymptotic first moment
nodes.statement: &\int_{-1}^1 t|\tilde{\Psi}_N(t)|^2 dt \\&=\mathcal{O}(N^{-2\delta})+\sum_{n=N+1}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor} \frac{2n+1}{8\pi^2r^2}|\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)|^2\left(\frac{n}{2n+1}\frac{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n-1)}{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)}+\frac{n+1}{2n+1}\frac{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n+1)}{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)}\right),\nonumber

nodes.name: Parameter choices versus the theoretical conditions
nodes.statement: Condition \eqref{eqn:ass1} suggests that the parameter $\beta_N$ should be significantly smaller than $\alpha_{N,n}$ and $\tilde{\alpha}_{N,n}$. This does not seem to be reflected by the parameters in Tables \ref{tab:err1} and \ref{tab:err2}. But Condition \eqref{eqn:propx} implies a relation between $N$ and $\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1$, $\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2$ that, for the choice $N=100$, leads to significantly smaller $\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1$, $\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2$ than those chosen in Tables \ref{tab:err1} and \ref{tab:err2}. Indeed, if we choose, e.g., $\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1=\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2=10^{-10}$ and repeat the above examples for $\rho=0.5$, we obtain a set of good parameters $\beta_N=10^{-6}$, $\alpha_{N,n}=10^4$, $\tilde{\alpha}_{N,n}=10^4$ that reflects the expected behaviour. However, our goal was to test realistic noise levels for the intended applications and show that the proposed method via optimized kernels works well for these scenarios.
nodes.statement_short: The tested parameters do not satisfy the theoretical conditions because realistic noise levels were used; with tiny noise the expected parameter behaviour appears.

nodes.name: Satellite and ground data $F_1$, $F_2$
nodes.statement: From satellite measurements we obtain data $F_1$ on a spherical orbit $\Omega_R=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^3:|x|=R\}$ and from ground or near-ground measurements data $F_2$ in a subregion $\Gamma_r$ of the spherical Earth surface $\Omega_r$ of radius $r<R$ (cf. Figure \ref{fig:datasit}).

nodes.name: Combined boundary value problem for harmonic potentials
nodes.statement_short: Find a harmonic $U$ outside $\Omega_r$ matching satellite data $F_1$ on $\Omega_R$ and ground data $F_2$ on $\Gamma_r$.

nodes.name: Restriction $U^+$
nodes.statement: Of interest to us is the restriction $U^+=U|_{\Gamma_r}$, i.e., the potential in the subregion $\Gamma_r$ of the Earth's surface.

nodes.name: Two-step approximation $U_N$
Scaling transform $T_N$ and scaling kernel $\Phi_N$
nodes.statement_short: $T_N$ is a regularized downward continuation acting as a scaling transform with band-limited kernel $\Phi_N$ of degree $N$.

nodes.name: Unit vectors $\xi$, $\eta$
nodes.statement: We frequently use $\xi$ and $\eta$ to abbreviate the unit vectors $\frac{x}{|x|}$ and $\frac{y}{|y|}$, respectively, and write $r=|x|$, $R=|y|$.

nodes.name: Orthonormal spherical harmonics $Y_{n,k}$
nodes.statement: Furthermore, $\{Y_{n,k}\}_{n=0,1,\ldots;k=1,\ldots,2n+1}$ denotes a set of orthonormal spherical harmonics of degree $n$ and order $k$.
also_stated_at: As mentioned in the introduction, $\{Y_{n,k}\}_{n=0,1,\ldots;k=1,\ldots,2n+1}$ denotes a set of orthonormal spherical harmonics of degree $n$ and order $k$.

nodes.name: Local wavelet operator $\tilde{W}_N$ and wavelet kernel $\tilde{\Psi}_N$
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde{W}_N$ is a wavelet transform on $\Gamma_r$ with kernel $\tilde{\Psi}_N$ of degree $\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor$, $\kappa>1$.

nodes.name: Symbols of kernels
nodes.statement: The coefficients ${\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)$ and $\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)$ are typically called 'symbols' of the corresponding kernels.

nodes.name: Sobolev space $\mathcal{H}_s(\Omega_r)$
nodes.statement_short: Sobolev space of $L^2(\Omega_r)$ functions with $\sum (n+1/2)^{2s}|F^\wedge(n,k)|^2<\infty$.

nodes.name: Space Pol$_N$ of band-limited zonal kernels
nodes.statement:
A further notion that we need is 
\begin{align} \textnormal{Pol}_{N}=\left\{K(x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}K^\wedge(n) Y_{n,k}\left(\xi\right)Y_{n,k}\left(\eta\right):K^\wedge(n)\in\mathbb{R}\right\},
\end{align}
the space of all band-limited zonal kernels with maximal degree $N$ (as always, $\xi$, $\eta$ denote the unit vectors $\frac{x}{|x|}$ and $\frac{y}{|y|}$, respectively).

nodes.name: Zonal kernel
nodes.statement:
Zonal means that $K$ only depends on the scalar product $\xi\cdot\eta$, more precisely,
\begin{align} K(x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\frac{2n+1}{4\pi}K^\wedge(n) P_n\left(\xi\cdot\eta\right),
\end{align}
with $P_n$ being the Legendre polynomial of degree $n$ (the expressions \eqref{polnj1} and \eqref{eqn:Kzonal} are connected by the spherical addition theorem).

nodes.name: Upward continuation
nodes.statement: Opposed to this, the determination of $F_1$ from $U^+$ is known as upward continuation.

nodes.name: Upward continuation operator $T^{up}$
nodes.statement:
The operator $T^{up}:L^2(\Omega_r)\to L^2(\Omega_R)$, given by
\begin{align} F_1(x)={T}^{up}[U^+](x)=\int_{\Omega_r}K^{up}(x,y) U^+(y)d\omega(y),\quad x\in\Omega_R,
\end{align}
with 
\begin{align} K^{up}(x,y)&=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}\sigma_n\frac{1}{R}Y_{n,k}\left(\xi\right)\frac{1}{r}Y_{n,k}\left(\eta\right)
\end{align}
and $\sigma_n=\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^n$, describes this process.

nodes.name: Downward continuation operator $T^{down}$
Admissibility conditions (a), (b) on scaling symbols
nodes.statement_short: Scaling symbols converge uniformly to $1/\sigma_n$ and are summable with weights $(2n+1)/4\pi$.

nodes.name: Bounded scaling transform $T_N$
Wavelet transform $W_N$
nodes.statement:
This operator can be refined further by use of the wavelet transform
\begin{align} {W}_N[F_1](x)=\int_{\Omega_R}\Psi_N(x,y) F_1(y)d\omega(y),\quad x\in\Omega_r,
\end{align}
where the kernel $\Psi_N$ is of the form \eqref{eqn:psin} with symbols $\Psi_N^\wedge(n)=\Phi_{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}^\wedge(n)-\Phi_N^\wedge(n)$.

nodes.name: Wavelet transform expressed via data on $\Omega_r$
nodes.statement:
Observing that $F_1$ and $F_2$ are only specific expressions of $U$ on the spheres $\Omega_R$ and $\Omega_r$, respectively, we find 
\begin{align} &\int_{\Omega_R}\Psi_N(x,y) F_1(y)d\omega(y)=\int_{\Omega_R}\Psi_N(x,y) U(y)d\omega(y)
\\&=\int_{\Omega_r}\tilde{\Psi}_N(x,y) U(y)d\omega(y)=\int_{\Omega_r}\tilde{\Psi}_N(x,y) F_2(y)d\omega(y),\quad x\in\Omega_r,\nonumber
\end{align}
where $\tilde{\Psi}_N$ is of the form \eqref{eqn:psin} with  $\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)=\sigma_n{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)=\Phi_{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}^\wedge(n)\sigma_n-\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n$ (the factor $\sigma_n$ stems from the downward continuation that occurs in the second equality of \eqref{eqn:Wjrr}).
nodes.section: 2.2 Combination of Downward Continuation and Local Data
nodes.statement_short: By harmonicity, convolving $F_1$ with $\Psi_N$ on $\Omega_R$ equals convolving $F_2$ with $\tilde{\Psi}_N$ on $\Omega_r$, with symbols multiplied by $\sigma_n$.
assumptions: $F_1$ and $F_2$ are only specific expressions of $U$ on the spheres $\Omega_R$ and $\Omega_r$, respectively

also_stated_at: They are coupled by the relation $\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)=\tilde{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)-{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)\big(\frac{r}{R}\big)^n$ (see Section \ref{subsec:comb} for details), where $\tilde{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)$ has been introduced as an auxiliary symbol.

nodes.name: Spherical cap $\mathcal{C}_r(x,\rho)$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{C}_r(x,\rho)$ denotes the spherical cap $\{y\in\Omega_r:1-\frac{x}{|x|}\cdot\frac{y}{|y|}<\rho\}$ with radius $\rho\in(0,2)$ and center $x\in\Omega_r$.

nodes.name: Subset $\tilde{\Gamma}_r$
nodes.statement: The subset $\tilde{\Gamma}_r\subset\Gamma_r$ is chosen such that $\mathcal{C}_r(x,\rho)\subset\Gamma_r$ for every $x\in\tilde{\Gamma}_r$ and some $\rho\in(0,2)$ that is fixed in advance.

nodes.name: Deterministic noise model
nodes.statement: From now on we assume contaminated input data $F_1^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1}=F_1+\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1E_1$ and $F_2^{\varepsilon_2}=F_2+\varepsilon_2E_2$ with deterministic noise $E_1\in L^2(\Omega_R)$, $E_2\in L^2(\Omega_r)$, and $\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1,\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2>0$.

nodes.name: Approximation from noisy data $U_N^\varepsilon$
Kernel design goal
nodes.statement: It is the aim of this paper to find kernels $\Phi_N$ and $\tilde{\Psi}_N$ (determined by the symbols $\Phi_N^\wedge(n)$ and $\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)=\tilde{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)-\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n$, respectively) that keep the error $\|U^+-U_N^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}$ small and allow some adaptations to possible a-priori knowledge on $F_1^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1}$ and $F_2^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2}$ (such as noise level of the measurements or data density).
nodes.statement_short: Find kernels $\Phi_N$, $\tilde{\Psi}_N$ that keep the approximation error on $\tilde{\Gamma}_r$ small and adapt to a-priori data knowledge.

nodes.name: Norm $\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\|_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}$
Overall error estimate
nodes.statement:
Similar estimates can be obtained for the terms $\varepsilon_1\|{T}_{N}[E_1]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}$ and $\varepsilon_2\|\tilde{W}_{N}[E_2]\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)}$ in \eqref{eqn:errorest2}, so that we end up with an overall estimate
\begin{align}
&\|U^+ - U_N^{\varepsilon}\|_{L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)} \\&\leq\|U^+\|_{\mathcal{H}_s(\Omega_r)}\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\frac{\big|1-\tilde{\Phi}_N^\wedge(n)\big|}{2\big(n+\frac{1}{2}\big)^s}+\|U^+\|_{\mathcal{H}_s(\Omega_r)}\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\frac{\big|1-{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\sigma_n\big|}{2\big(n+\frac{1}{2}\big)^s}\nonumber
\\&\quad+\varepsilon_1\|E_1\|_{L^2(\Omega_R)}\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\big|\Phi_{N}^\wedge(n)\big|
+\Big(\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2\|E_2\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}+\frac{1}{2}\|U^+\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}\Big)\sup_{n=0,1,\ldots}\big|\tilde{\Psi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\big|\nonumber
\\&\quad+2\sqrt{2}\pi r^2\left(\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2\|E_2\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}+\|U^+\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}\right)\big\|\tilde{\Psi}_{N}\big\|_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}.\nonumber
\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The $L^2(\tilde{\Gamma}_r)$ error is bounded by symbol-dependent terms for approximation, downward continuation, noise and localization.
conclusions: we end up with an overall estimate

nodes.name: Minimization of the functional $\mathcal{F}$
nodes.statement_short: Choose symbols minimizing a weighted sum of approximation, downward-continuation, symbol-norm and localization penalties over band-limited kernels.

nodes.name: Parameters $\tilde{\alpha}_{N,n}$, $\alpha_{N,n}$, $\beta_N$
nodes.statement: All pre-factors appearing in \eqref{eqn:errorestfinal} have been compensated into the parameters $\tilde{\alpha}_{N,n}$, ${\alpha}_{N,n}$, and $\beta_N$.

nodes.name: Normalized localization measure
nodes.statement_short: A more suitable localization measure is the ratio of the kernel's norm outside the cap to its total norm.

nodes.name: Shannon-type reference approximation $U_M^{\varepsilon,Sh}$
Optimized kernels outperform Shannon-type kernels
nodes.statement: Tables  \ref{tab:err1} and \ref{tab:err2} show that the optimized kernels behave better than the Shannon-type kernels over the broad range of settings.

nodes.name: Pure downward continuation performs worst
nodes.statement: In Table \ref{tab:err4} we can see that for our test example pure downward continuation from satellite data on $\Omega_R$ yields significantly worse results than all other tested methods.

nodes.name: Vectorial boundary value problem
nodes.statement_short: Find the gradient $b=\nabla U$ of a harmonic potential from vector data on $\Omega_R$ and $\Gamma_r$.

nodes.name: Restriction $b^+$
nodes.statement: Starting from equations \eqref{eqn:bvp441}--\eqref{eqn:bvp444}, the general procedure for approximating $b^+=b|_{\Gamma_r}$  is essentially the same as for the scalar case treated in the previous sections.

nodes.name: Vector spherical harmonics $y^{(i)}_{n,k}$
Surface gradient $\nabla^*_\xi$
nodes.statement:
The operator $
abla^*_\xi$ denotes the surface gradient, i.e., the tangential contribution of the gradient $
abla_x$ (more precisely, $
abla_x=\xi rac{\partial}{\partial{r}}+ rac{1}{r}
abla^*_{\xi}$, with $\xi= rac{x}{|x|}$ and $r=|x|$).

nodes.name: Surface curl gradient $L^*_\xi$
nodes.statement: The surface curl gradient $L^*_{\xi}$ stands short for $\xi\wedge\nabla_{\xi}^*$ (with $\wedge$ being the vector product of two vectors $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^3$).

nodes.name: Vector spherical harmonics form an orthonormal basis of $l^2(\Omega)$
nodes.statement: Together, the functions \eqref{eqn:ynk1}--\eqref{eqn:ynk3} form an orthonormal basis of the space $l^2(\Omega)$ of vectorial functions that are square-integrable on the unit sphere.
conclusions: the functions \eqref{eqn:ynk1}--\eqref{eqn:ynk3} form an orthonormal basis of the space $l^2(\Omega)$ of vectorial functions that are square-integrable on the unit sphere

nodes.name: Tensorial Legendre polynomials
Tensor product $\otimes$
nodes.statement: The operator $\otimes$ denotes the tensor product $x\otimes y=xy^T$ of two vectors $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^3$.

nodes.name: Vectorial Sobolev space $\mathfrak{h}_s(\Omega_r)$
nodes.statement_short: Vectorial Sobolev space of $l^2(\Omega_r)$ fields with weighted summable type-1 and type-2 Fourier coefficients.

nodes.name: Space $\mathbf{Pol}_N$ of band-limited tensorial kernels
Tensor-zonal kernels
nodes.statement: The kernels $\mathbf{Pol}_{N}$ are tensor-zonal. In particular, this means that the absolute value $|{\mathbf{K}}(x,y)|$ depends only on the scalar product $\xi\cdot\eta$ (this does not have to hold true for the kernel ${\mathbf{K}}(x,y)$ itself).

nodes.name: Vectorial upward and downward continuation operators
nodes.statement: Similar to the scalar case in Subsection \ref{subsec:dc}, there is a vectorial upward continuation operator $t^{up}$ and a vectorial downward continuation operator $t^{down}$, defined via tensorial kernels with singular values $\sigma_n=\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^{n+1}$ and $\frac{1}{\sigma_n}$, respectively (note that in the scalar case, $\sigma_n=\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^{n}$).

nodes.name: Vectorial scaling transform $t_N$
Conditions (a), (b) for vectorial scaling symbols
nodes.statement: The symbols $\mathbf{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)$ need to satisfy the same conditions (a), (b) as for the scalar analogue in Subsection \ref{subsec:dc}.

nodes.name: Vectorial wavelet operator $\tilde{w}_N$
Conditions (a'), (b') for vectorial auxiliary symbols
nodes.statement: The symbols $\tilde{ \mathbf{\Phi}}_{N}^\wedge(n)$ are assumed to satisfy conditions $($a'$)$ and $($b'$)$ from Subsection \ref{subsec:comb}.

nodes.name: Vectorial deterministic noise model
nodes.statement: As in the scalar case, the input data $f_1$, $f_2$ is perturbed by deterministic noise $e_1\in l^2(\Omega_R)$ and $e_2\in l^2(\Omega_r)$, so that we are dealing with $f_1^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1}=f_1+\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_1 e_1$ and $f_2^{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2}=f_2+\ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2 e_2$.

nodes.name: Vectorial approximation $b_N^\varepsilon$
Minimization of the vectorial functional
nodes.statement_short: Choose tensorial symbols minimizing the vectorial analogue of $\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: Penalty in Gram form
nodes.statement:
First we observe that the representation \eqref{eqn:psin} of the kernel $\tilde{\Psi}_N$ and its zonality together with the addition theorem for spherical harmonics imply 
\small
\begin{align} &8\pi^2 r^4\left\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\right\|^2_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}
\\&=\frac{8\pi^2 r^4}{r^4}\int_{-1}^{1-\rho}\Bigg|\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{2n+1}{4\pi}\left(\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)-\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n\right)P_n(t)\Bigg|^2dt\nonumber
\\&=\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\sum_{m=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{(2n+1)(2m+1)}{2}\left(\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(m)-\Phi_N^\wedge(m)\sigma_m\right)\left(\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)-\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n\right)\int_{-1}^{1-\rho}\!\!\!\!\!\!\!P_n(t)P_m(t)dt\nonumber
\\&=\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\sum_{m=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\left(\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(m)-\Phi_N^\wedge(m)\sigma_m\right)\left(\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)-\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n\right)P_{n,m}^\rho.\nonumber
\end{align}
\normalsize
nodes.statement_short: Express the localization penalty via symbols and the Gram entries $P^\rho_{n,m}$

nodes.name: Differentiate functional
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the functional with respect to the symbols

nodes.name: Normal equations
nodes.statement: Setting the two expressions above equal to zero, a proper reordering leads to the linear equation \eqref{eqn:lineq1}.
nodes.statement_short: Set derivatives to zero to obtain the linear system

nodes.name: Positive definiteness
nodes.statement: At last, we observe that the matrix $(P_{n,m}^\rho)_{n,m=0,\ldots,\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}$ is positive definite (since it represents a Gram matrix of linearly independent functions) and that all appearing diagonal matrices are positive definite due to positive matrix entries. Thus, the matrix $\mathbf{M}$ is positive definite and the linear system \eqref{eqn:lineq1} is uniquely solvable and leads to a minimum of \eqref{eqn:mineq2}.
nodes.statement_short: Positive definiteness gives unique solvability and a minimum

nodes.name: Shannon-type kernels
nodes.statement_short: Introduce Shannon-type comparison kernels

nodes.name: Functional at Shannon kernels
nodes.statement_short: Bound the functional at the Shannon kernels

nodes.name: Compare with minimizer
nodes.statement_short: Minimality bounds each weighted symbol error by the Shannon value

nodes.name: Symbol rates
nodes.statement:
In combination with \eqref{eqn:ass1}, this leads to
\begin{align} \big|1-\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)\big|= \mathcal{O}(N^{-1-\delta}),
\end{align}
uniformly for all $n\leq \lfloor\kappa N\rfloor$ and $N\to\infty$. The estimate $|1-\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n|=\mathcal{O}(N^{-1-\delta})$ follows in the same manner and holds uniformly for all $n\leq N$ and $N\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Derive the rate $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1-\delta})$ for symbol errors

nodes.name: First two terms vanish
nodes.statement_short: First and second error terms vanish

nodes.name: Third term vanishes
nodes.statement_short: Noise term on $\Omega_R$ vanishes by the noise coupling condition

nodes.name: Fourth term
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the fourth term to a wavelet-symbol sum that vanishes

nodes.name: Reduce localization term
nodes.statement:
In order to handle the last term of the error estimate \eqref{eqn:errorestfinal}, it has to be shown that $\|\tilde{\Psi}_N\|_{L^2([-1,1-\rho])}$ tends to zero. This, again, is generally not true. But, taking a closer look at the derivation of the estimate indicates that it suffices to show that
\small\begin{align} \Bigg\|\,\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\tilde{\Psi}_{N}(\cdot,y) U^+(y)d\omega(y)\Bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}, \qquad \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_2\Bigg\|\,\,\int_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(\rho,\cdot)}\tilde{\Psi}_{N}(\cdot,y) E_2(y)d\omega(y)\Bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega_r)}
\end{align}\normalsize
vanish as $N\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the localization term to two integrals outside the cap

nodes.name: Apply Riemann localization
nodes.statement_short: Split via Shannon kernel and apply Proposition 4.2 with Young's inequality

nodes.name: Distance to Shannon kernel
nodes.statement_short: Bound the distance to the Shannon kernel by $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2\delta})$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: For the right expression in \eqref{eqn:altterms}, we obtain the desired result in a similar but easier manner. Finally, combining all steps of the proof, we have shown that the right hand side of the error estimate \eqref{eqn:errorestfinal} converges to zero, which yields \eqref{eqn:convres}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine all terms to conclude convergence

nodes.name: Cantelli bound
nodes.statement_short: Treat normalized kernel as density and apply Cantelli's inequality

nodes.name: Notation
nodes.statement: By $P_N(t< a)$ we mean the probability (with respect to the density function $F_N$) that $t$ lies in the interval $[-1,a)$ while $P_N(t\geq a)$ means the probability of $t$ being in the interval $[a,1]$. Furthermore, $E_N(t)$ denotes the expected value of $t$ and $V_N(t)=E(t^2)-(E(t))^2$ the variance of $t$.
nodes.statement_short: Define probability, mean and variance notation

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: In other words, we are done if we can show that $\lim_{N\to\infty}E_N(t)=1$ and $\lim_{N\to \infty}V_N(t)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to mean tending to 1 and variance to 0

nodes.name: First moment
nodes.statement:
First, we use the addition theorem for spherical harmonics and the recurrence relation  $tP_n(t)=\frac{1}{2n+1}\left((n+1)P_{n+1}(t)+nP_{n-1}(t)\right)$ to obtain  
\begin{align} \int_{-1}^1 t|\tilde{\Psi}_N(t)|^2 dt&= \frac{1}{r^2} \sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\sum_{m=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{2n+1}{4\pi}\frac{2m+1}{4\pi}\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(m)\int_{-1}^1tP_n(t)P_m(t)dt
\\&=\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\frac{2n+1}{16\pi^2r^2}\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)\left(n\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n-1)+(n+1)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n+1)\right)\int_{-1}^1|P_n(t)|^2 dt\nonumber
\\&=\frac{1}{8\pi^2r^2}\sum_{n=0}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}n\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n-1)+(n+1)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n+1).\nonumber
\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Compute the first moment via the Legendre recurrence

nodes.name: Asymptotic first moment
nodes.statement:
From \eqref{eqn:conphij} and the corresponding estimate for $\Phi_N^\wedge(n)\sigma_n$ we find $|\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)|^2=\mathcal{O}(N^{-2(1+\delta)})$ for $n\leq N$, and $|1-\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)|^2=|1-\tilde{\Phi}_{N}^\wedge(n)|^2=\mathcal{O}(N^{-2(1+\delta)})$, for $N+1\leq n\leq \lfloor\kappa N\rfloor$. As a consequence,  \eqref{eqn:et1} implies
\begin{align} &\int_{-1}^1 t|\tilde{\Psi}_N(t)|^2 dt
\\&=\mathcal{O}(N^{-2\delta})+\sum_{n=N+1}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor} \frac{2n+1}{8\pi^2r^2}|\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)|^2\left(\frac{n}{2n+1}\frac{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n-1)}{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)}+\frac{n+1}{2n+1}\frac{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n+1)}{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)}\right),\nonumber
\end{align}
where $\sup_{N+1\leq n\leq\lfloor \kappa N\rfloor}\big|1-\big(\frac{n}{2n+1}{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n-1)}/{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)}+\frac{n+1}{2n+1}{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n+1)}/{\tilde{\Psi}_N^\wedge(n)}\big)\big|\leq\varepsilon_N$, for  some $\varepsilon_N>0$ that satisfies $\varepsilon_N\to0$ as $N\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Use symbol rates to simplify the first moment asymptotically

nodes.name: Kernel norm
nodes.statement_short: Express the kernel norm similarly

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Mean tends to 1; analogously variance tends to 0

nodes.name: Expansion
nodes.statement:
We first observe that
\begin{align} &\int\limits_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(x,\rho)}\tilde{\mathbf{\Psi}}^{Sh}_{N}(x,y) f(y)d\omega(y)
\\&=\int\limits_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(x,\rho)}\left(\sum_{i=1}^2\sum_{n=N+1}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}\frac{1}{r}y_{n,k}^{(i)}\left(\xi\right)\otimes \frac{1}{r}y_{n,k}^{(i)}\left(\eta\right)\right) f(r\eta)d\omega(r\eta)\nonumber
\\&=\sum_{i=1}^2\sum_{n=N+1}^{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}\sum_{k=1}^{2n+1}\frac{1}{r}y_{n,k}^{(i)}\left(\xi\right)\int\limits_{\Omega_r\setminus\mathcal{C}_r(x,\rho)}\frac{1}{r}y_{n,k}^{(i)}\left(\eta\right)\cdot f(r\eta)d\omega(r\eta),\nonumber
\end{align}
where, as always, $\xi=\frac{x}{|x|}$ and $\eta=\frac{y}{|y|}$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the localization integral of the Shannon kernel
